questions.question: In the Classroom/Student example, what is `ClassroomId` on `Student`?
options: The foreign key — the actual column linking a student row to its classroom row
The same thing as the navigation property Classroom
questions.explanation: ClassroomId is the real foreign key column stored in the database. `Classroom` (the navigation property) is a C#-only convenience for accessing the related object without a manual lookup.

questions.question: What prints, given a classroom that genuinely has 2 students already saved in the database?
options: 0 — related data isn't loaded automatically without Include
questions.explanation: EF Core does NOT automatically load navigation properties (no automatic lazy loading by default). Without `.Include(c => c.Students)`, the Students collection is simply empty, even though matching rows exist in the database.

questions.question: What does `.Include(c => c.Students)` do?
options: Filters classrooms to only ones with students
Tells EF Core to also load the Students navigation property in the same query
Adds a new student to the classroom
Deletes students not matching a condition
questions.explanation: Include is how you explicitly ask EF Core to eager-load a related navigation property — without it, that property stays empty even when related rows exist.

questions.question: You need every Student in a specific classroom, without loading the whole Classroom object. What's a reasonable approach?
options: You must always use Include on Classrooms
Query the Students DbSet directly: `context.Students.Where(s => s.ClassroomId == classroomId).ToListAsync()`
This is impossible in EF Core
Load every student in the database, then filter in C#
questions.explanation: You can query from either side of a relationship — going directly to the 'many' side's DbSet and filtering by the foreign key is often simpler than loading the 'one' side with Include.

questions.question: Adding students to `classroom.Students` and saving the whole graph together means you don't need to manually set each student's ClassroomId.
questions.explanation: EF Core works out the foreign key values automatically when you save a connected object graph through its navigation properties — you don't need to wire up the ClassroomId by hand.

questions.question: Deleting a Classroom that students depend on (a required relationship) has no effect on the related Student rows by default.
questions.explanation: By default, EF Core cascades the delete — removing a Classroom also removes its dependent Student rows, since a Student can't exist without a Classroom when the foreign key is required (non-nullable).
